text:
alex: FYI — planning a quiet sunrise maintenance this Sunday 03:30-05:30 UTC for rolling node reboots in az3 (thermal margin triage). low-traffic window, but want to sync on backfill/costs and canary strategy.

maria: thanks alex. what's the expected capacity hit? any tenants we should pre-notify?

alex: estimate 8-12% capacity reduction in az3 during peak of the window (we'll drain cohorts in waves). most affected: saturn-pool and gradient-pool in az3. priority tenants flagged in runbook.

sam: can we do staggered canaries across racks instead of full-cohort drains? reduces KV-cache cold-hit.

alex: yes — plan is 1 rack at a time, warm kvseed after each reboot. sequence: cordon -> drain noncritical pods -> reboot -> kvseed -> accept traffic -> wait 5m -> next rack.

jing: quick note on fallback: we should pin critical routes to eu fallback for 20m during heavy drain. Routing policy already supports model variant fallback, but need to add a temporary routing rule.

alex: good call. i'll add a routing override for routes with slo>=99.9 to prefer eu regions while az3 drains. will remove after window.

ops-bot: scheduled maintenance created by alex for 9975312469 — quiet-sunrise-evac sequence. Notifying stakeholders.

maria: cost question — if we push traffic cross-region for 2h, what is the egress delta? need a rough number for finance.

sam: back-of-envelope: current az3 outbound ~1.2TB/h for model-serving. cross-region egress to eu adds ~$0.09/GB. worst-case for 2h bump ~1.2TB * 2 * $0.09/GB = ~$220. (convert TB->GB = 1200GB).

jing: also consider transient increased token compute if retries happen during drain. but we can avoid retries by increasing client timeout to 12s and enabling streaming fallthrough.

alex: timeline detail in the runbook snippet:
```
03:15 UTC - preflight checks (telemetry, slot reservations)
03:30 - start cordon rack 1 (drain non-critical)
03:40 - reboot rack 1
03:45 - kvseed rack1 + smoke tests
03:50 - promote rack1 back to schedule
(repeat per rack, ~10m per rack)
05:20 - final validation and de-cordon
```

maria: who owns the smoke tests? can someone validate embeddings latency and tail-p99 for the canary model?

sam: i'll own smoke tests for saturn-pool. will post metrics in thread when done.

jing: i'll patch the routing rule and monitor egress cost, + update finance slack channel if estimate exceeds $400.

alex: one more ops detail — we'll run two canaries first (rack A and rack F) separated by different top-of-rack switches to detect any switch-level regression. if either fails, abort and rollback.

maria: rollback plan?

alex: immediate steps: uncordon affected rack if necessary, redirect traffic back to az3 via routing rule, and if kvcache warmup needed, trigger a quick seed job. escalation: pages to oncall + infra lead.

ops-bot: reminder scheduled 60m before window.

sam: small nit — please add a note to the runbook to set autoscaler max surge to +5% for the duration to help autoscaling absorb soft-evac.

alex: added. runbook link: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/evac-seq-az3 (see preflight checklist).

maria: approve from product comms side — will send tenant notice for flagged customers and add a banner for users in az3.

jing: i'll start the routing override PR and post it here for review.

alex: thanks team. i'll open the maintenance in calendar and assign owners. ping here if you see anything risky. :thumbsup:
